name: Common kidney problems in children and bed wetting

content.text: Dr Iqtidar said, "Urinary tract infections are common in infants and children. Some children have underlying congenital anomalies and stone diseases. These infections require early detection, investigations and management to avoid morbidity and mortality in later years. Similarly nephrotic syndrome is a very common disease entity, which presents with remissions and relapses and does not have a specified end point. It affects children 2-6 years old. They leak protein from their kidneys and present with swelling of face, abdomen and whole body. Nephrotic syndrome is much common in our country than in the west." Dr Iqtidar added that Stone disease is also common in our country. Both kidney and urinary bladder stones cause a lot of suffering in young children. Besides operative treatment, they can now be removed by Extracorporeal Shock Wave Lithotripsy (ESWL).

Dr Iqtidar said, "Bedwetting (nocturnal enuresis) is another common problem of children. Almost 10 percent of 5 year old and 5 percent of 1 0 year old suffer from this problem. Children usually grow out of this problem. Generally, there is a family history of bedwetting (nocturnal enuresis). These children suffer at the hands of their parents, siblings, friends, etc. They lack self-confidence and self esteem. They can be helped in several ways. A nasal spray (desmopressin) is now licensed for use in nocturnal enuresis."

Dr Iqtidar concluded by saying that it is about time that we should preserve our meager resources and prevent renal disease from early childhood rather than opening more dialysis and transplant centres. The future demands in giving Paediatric Nephrology a chance, training paediatric nephrologists and opening paediatric nephrology units in all leaching hospitals.

content.author: volunteer.pa
content.description: "Almost half of our population consists of children less than 18 years. The life span of people has increased from 43 years to 64 years over the last three decades. Similarly death rate and infant mortality have reduced. Although, we have several adult nephrology units, but there is not a single paediatric nephrology unit in the country", informed Dr Iqtidar Ahmad Khan, Consultant Paediatrician, Paediatric Nephrologist and Associate Professor of Paediatrics, The Aga Khan University Hospital. He was giving a presentation on "Common Kidney Problems in Children and Bed Wetting" at Signs, Symptoms and Care', monthly health awareness program, held on September 25, 1999.
